entries.what: a handle is the one two-valued thing a region can carry, density buys nothing, and a cavity is not a handle

findings.name: b₁ of a solid block, at every size

expect.of: 0 — DENSITY BUYS NOTHING
expect.because: a solid block is contractible however large, so piling up cells cannot produce the bit a particle needs — which is why the argument had to go to topology rather than to size

expect.of: 1 — one handle, one bit
expect.because: a region the lattice goes ROUND rather than through, and one bit each is all homology has to offer

expect.of: 2 — handles add
expect.because: which is what makes the count an invariant rather than a yes or no

findings.name: b₁ of a hollow shell

expect.of: 0 — A CAVITY IS NOT A HANDLE
expect.because: removing a ball from a solid leaves it simply connected: the void is b₂ and shows up there instead. This is the control that says the two are being told apart rather than a hole of any kind being counted.

findings.note: its b₂ is 1, which is where a sealed void belongs

entries.what: a body that redirects the vacuum's own rays moves, and one that emits evenly does not — with the absorbed and emitted momentum both counted

findings.name: QUICK RUN
findings.note: measured at a reduced box and tick count. Good enough to say whether something broke; NOT good enough to quote — a published number is a `full` run.

findings.name: control: an even emitter goes nowhere

expect.of: nought — every exit has its opposite, so what leaves cancels
expect.because: if this is not zero the measurement has a bias in it and no other row means anything

findings.name: backward: does redirecting the vacuum push it forward?

expect.of: POSITIVE — rays sent behind, so the recoil is forward
expect.because: this is the reading in which a thing moves by rearranging the space it is already in, rather than by making anything

findings.note: 170.2σ against the control

findings.name: forward: rocket or shadow?
findings.note: NEGATIVE means the recoil wins and it behaves like a rocket. POSITIVE means the shadow wins — the vacuum ahead is thinned by its own emission and the pressure behind pushes it INTO the direction it is emitting, which is the gravity mechanism turned around.

expect.of: nought — a ray passed straight through carries the same momentum out as in
expect.because: which is the control that says this can tell a redirection from a pass-through, rather than calling any rearrangement a push

findings.name: does it need to CREATE rays, or only move them?
findings.note: the conserving row emits only as many rays as it caught, so it makes nothing. Near 1 means the vacuum alone is enough and the push is a redirection; near 0 means the push was coming from rays made out of nothing, which is not propulsion.

findings.name: gravity's growth over the conserving medium's

expect.of: well above 1 — the loop is a large effect, not a correction

entries.what: the vacuum settles at (1−p)/(2−p) with the rate cancelling out, and a polarised one settles below it because (G+M/1) is a sink the derivation has no term for

findings.name: spread over a 12× change in the rate

expect.of: small — the rate cancels out of the fixed point
expect.because: f → p + (1−p)f then f(1−p) has the rate cancelling; adding annihilation breaks that, because creation scales with p and destruction scales with density

expect.of: the fixed point of edging and thinning
expect.because: with nothing destroying anything, creation and thinning are the whole of what moves the occupancy, and this is their fixed point

findings.name: mean free path (cells)
findings.note: 1/fill — a ray meets something when it lands where one sits on the opposing exit. EVERY screening length in this book is this number, so it is reported here rather than re-derived wherever it is needed.

findings.name: spread over a 12× change in the rate

expect.of: LARGE — with a sink in it, the balance depends on how fast the rule is run
expect.because: f → p + (1−p)f then f(1−p) has the rate cancelling; adding annihilation breaks that, because creation scales with p and destruction scales with density

findings.name: occupancy over (1−p)/(2−p)

expect.of: WELL BELOW 1 — this theory annihilates, and the derivation has no term for it
expect.because: annihilation is a sink f → p + (1−p)f then f(1−p) does not contain, so a theory that destroys cannot sit at the fixed point of one that does not

findings.note: which means the ½ this book quotes as 'the vacuum's derived occupancy' is the occupancy of a medium NEITHER of its theories is — and since every screening length here is a mean free path, that is worth more than a factor of two.

entries.what: the reading of what counts as a meeting decides the vacuum's occupancy, and therefore whether any force in this model is measurable at all

findings.name: QUICK RUN
findings.note: measured at a reduced box and tick count. Good enough to say whether something broke; NOT good enough to quote — a published number is a `full` run.

findings.name: readings that resolve an attraction at all

expect.because: two bodies drawing together is the one thing every version of this model has agreed on, so it is the test a reading of the rules has to pass

findings.note: strongest: head-on/all at 8.5σ

findings.name: the default reading's attraction

expect.of: positive and resolved — co-located, one meeting a point a tick
expect.because: this is what the article's sentence says: any two rays that arrive together have met, and what is left is A SINGLE neutral point

findings.note: 1.5σ · fill 0.027 · mean free path 36.7 cells

findings.name: what pulsing costs, under the default reading
findings.note: inert -9.53e-1 at 1.5σ against pulsing -1.10e+0 at 1.2σ. A body that pulses spends itself emitting its own rays instead of passing the vacuum's along, which is what being massive costs; a body that does not is carried by what the expansion sends it.

findings.name: spread in occupancy across the four readings
findings.note: how far apart four readings of one sentence put the vacuum — and since every screening length here is 1/fill, this is the factor by which the range of every force in this model depends on a choice nobody had written down
